boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places for studying, making, recording, gathering, viewing art, and using recreation resources, each supported by a current Sonoma State source.

cards.title: University Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: University Library · quiet study space
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from a quieter setting, then use the floor’s study areas or head to the Quiet Study Room when you need added focus.
cards.short_summary: A quieter library floor for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library identifies its third floor as a place for peace and quiet and directs visitors to the Quiet Study Room for an extra-quiet spot.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Jean and Charles Schulz Information Center; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Quiet Study Room
cards.subtitle: University Library third floor
cards.notes: Choose this room when you need an extra-quiet stretch of reading or writing; keep conversations and group work for the library’s more active floors.
cards.short_summary: The library’s designated extra-quiet study option.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library’s study-spaces page names the Quiet Study Room as an extra-quiet spot on the third floor.
cards.access_notes: On the University Library’s third floor; visit during posted library hours.

cards.title: SSU Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: University Library · Jean and Charles Schulz Information Center
cards.notes: Drop in to explore fabrication and prototyping tools, or look for a workshop. Ask staff for guidance before using unfamiliar equipment.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on library space for experimenting, prototyping, and making.
cards.evidence_claim: SSU says its Library Makerspace supports digital fabrication, prototyping, workshops, and cross-disciplinary collaboration; access and equipment use are free for SSU affiliates.
cards.access_notes: For Sonoma State students, staff, and faculty during posted hours; some large projects may require users to supply materials.

cards.title: Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Maker Commons · University Library 2 South
cards.notes: Use a high-performance workstation for editing, design, 3D modeling, or data-heavy projects; no reservation is required for the lab.
cards.short_summary: Ten workstations for digital projects and large data sets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Media Lab has 10 high-performance workstations for digital creation, editing, 3D modeling, graphic design, and data analysis, with no reservations required.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Maker Commons in 2 South; use during posted library hours and sign in with SSU credentials for applicable software.

cards.title: Media Production Studios
cards.subtitle: University Library · Schulz 2020B and 2021
cards.notes: Book an audio or video studio for a recorded project, then save files to personal storage and leave the equipment and room ready for the next user.
cards.short_summary: Bookable library studios for audio and video production.
cards.evidence_claim: SSU’s Media Production Studios offer professional audio and video equipment, editing Macs, and no-cost booking for SSU students, faculty, and staff when the library is open.
cards.access_notes: Booking is required; available to SSU students, faculty, and staff whenever the library is open.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Student Center first floor
cards.notes: Set up by the fireplace for a study session, bring friends for board games, or use the couches for a break between campus commitments.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center lounge for studying, board games, and relaxing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center describes the Living Room as a place to study, enjoy board games, or relax with friends, with couches and a fireplace.
cards.access_notes: A Student Center public-use space; it cannot be reserved for programming, tabling, or soliciting.

cards.title: Seawolf Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between the Student Center and Recreation Center
cards.notes: Meet outside between classes, watch the LoboVision display, or use the plaza for a properly reserved campus event with any needed support arranged ahead.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Student Center–Recreation Center gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Sonoma State locates Seawolf Plaza between the Student Center and Recreation Center and identifies LoboVision on the Recreation Center’s east wall as a plaza feature.
cards.access_notes: The plaza and LoboVision can be reserved for events; campus closures and breaks affect scheduled plaza music.

cards.title: University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: College of Humanities, Social Sciences, and the Arts
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar before you go, then spend time with the current work or attend a listed public program or artist-focused event.
cards.short_summary: Campus gallery for contemporary exhibitions and student shows.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Art Gallery presents modern and contemporary exhibitions, public programs, artist talks, and annual student exhibitions.
cards.source_title: University Art Gallery at Sonoma State University
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday during exhibitions only; the gallery notes temporary summer closure dates and campus parking requirements.

cards.title: Campus Recreation Climbing Wall
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation Center
cards.notes: Check the current climbing-wall schedule before planning a visit, and follow staff direction and facility procedures when the wall is operating.
cards.short_summary: A 39-foot roped wall with top-rope, lead, and bouldering terrain.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation describes a 39-foot roped Climbing Wall with 11 top ropes, bolted lead lines, and a top-out boulder.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on Recreation Center membership and current wall hours; the current Campus Recreation page lists climbing-wall hours separately.

cards.title: Outdoor Resource Center
cards.subtitle: Behind the Campus Recreation front desk
cards.notes: Stop by for trail maps and bike tools, or ask about the outdoor-resource library and rental options when planning an equipment-supported outing.
cards.short_summary: A Recreation Center resource point for trail information, tools, and gear.
cards.evidence_claim: The Outdoor Resource Center is behind the Campus Recreation front desk and provides free outdoor-resource libraries, bike tools, and trail maps, plus affordable rentals.
cards.access_notes: Located behind the Campus Recreation front desk; check current Outdoor Resource Center hours and any rental requirements before visiting.
